facts.claim: A demon named Vaka (Bakasura) ruled the town and country near Ekachakra, living on human flesh.

sources.quote: there liveth a Rakshasa of the name of Vaka, which cannibal is the lord of this country and town

facts.claim: The tribute fixed for the demon was a cart-load of rice, two buffaloes, and a human being to carry it to him.

sources.quote: a cart-load of rice, two buffaloes, and a human being who conveyeth them unto him

facts.claim: Householders took turns sending the tribute, and a family's turn came only after many long years.

sources.quote: The turn, however, cometh to a particular family at intervals of many long years.

facts.claim: Anyone who tried to dodge the tribute was killed by the demon along with their family.

sources.quote: If there are any that seek to avoid it, the Rakshasa slayeth them with their children and wives and devoureth them all.

facts.claim: The Pandavas were living disguised in the house of a Brahmana at Ekachakra when the tribute turn fell on their host.

sources.quote: those mighty car-warriors, the sons of Kunti, on arriving at Ekachakra, lived for a short time in the abode of a Brahmana

facts.claim: Bhima alone ate half of all the food the Pandavas collected while begging.

sources.quote: the mighty Bhima alone took the other moiety

facts.claim: Kunti offered one of her five sons to go to the demon in the Brahmana's place.

sources.quote: I have five sons, O Brahmana, let one of them go, carrying in thy behalf tribute of that Rakshasa.

facts.claim: Kunti told the Brahmana that Bhima was immensely strong and would not be killed by the demon.

sources.quote: this Rakshasa will not be able to kill my son, for that son of mine is endued with great prowess and energy

facts.claim: Bhima accepted the task with the words 'So be it.'

sources.quote: Bhima replied unto them, saying, 'So be it.'

facts.claim: Bhima carried the demon's food to the forest and began eating it himself while calling the demon by name.

sources.quote: began to eat himself the food he carried, calling loudly to the Rakshasa by name

facts.claim: The demon arrived to find Bhima eating the food intended for him.

sources.quote: Beholding Bhima eating his food, the Rakshasa advanced, biting his nether lip and expanding his eyes in wrath.

facts.claim: The demon demanded to know who was eating his food in front of him.

sources.quote: Who is this fool, who desiring to go to the abode of Yama, eateth in my very sight the food intended for me?

facts.claim: Bhima smiled in derision and kept eating without looking up, even after the demon struck him on the back.

sources.quote: did not even look up at the Rakshasa but continued to eat as before

facts.claim: Bhima finished the whole meal, washed, and then stood up cheerfully to fight.

sources.quote: had leisurely eaten up the whole of that food and washing himself stood cheerfully for fight

facts.claim: The fight began with the two hurling trees at each other until the area was stripped of trees.

sources.quote: the combat with trees between that human being and the Rakshasa, became so terrible that the region around soon became destitute of trees

facts.claim: Bhima finally broke the demon's back across his knee, and the demon died.

sources.quote: Then Vaka, huge as a mountain, thus broken (on Bhima’s knee), died, uttering frightful yells.

facts.claim: Bhima made the dead demon's relatives promise to stop killing human beings.

sources.quote: Do not ever again kill human beings. If ye kill men, ye will have to die even as Vaka.

facts.claim: Bhima dragged the dead demon to a town gate and left, unseen by anyone.

sources.quote: Then Bhima, dragging the lifeless cannibal, placed him at one of the gates of the town and went away unobserved by any one.

facts.claim: In the morning the townspeople found the demon dead and were astonished at the feat.

sources.quote: The next morning the inhabitants of the town in coming out saw the Rakshasa lying dead on the ground

facts.claim: The Brahmana hid the truth, crediting a nameless mantra-skilled Brahmana with carrying the food and killing the demon.

sources.quote: A certain high-souled Brahmana, skilled in mantras, beheld me weeping with my relatives after I had been ordered to supply the Rakshasa’s food.

facts.claim: The townspeople established a festival in remembrance of their deliverance.

sources.quote: they all established a festival in which the worship of Brahmanas was the principal ceremony

facts.claim: The demon is described as huge, red-eyed, red-bearded, with a mouth stretching ear to ear.

sources.quote: Of huge body and great strength, of red eyes, red beard, and red hair, he was terrible to behold
